li.label: sent a letter home
li.description: A scribe wrote down what I wanted to say, every word of it. It goes out with the next rider headed that way.

li.label: our story written down
li.description: The colony's story is written out fair and bound in leather. Someone will read it long after we're gone.

li.label: our picture on the wall
li.description: There's a picture of all of us on the wall now. I look at it every time I walk past.

li.label: a glitterworlder's questions
li.description: The glitterworld tourist asked three times where our water comes from, and wrote the answer down every time.

li.label: a glitterworlder in the barn
li.description: I watched a rich tourist from a glitterworld muck out our barn, complaining with every forkful.

li.label: the spirit-singer's song
li.description: A spirit-singer sang to the land by our fire, one long song with the drum under it. I can still hear the drum.

li.label: our dead were sung to
li.description: A singer went from grave to grave in the dusk and sang each of our dead a short song of its own.

li.label: a traveling cook's feast
li.description: A traveling cook took over our kitchen for a day and made the best meal I've had in years, out of our own stores.

li.label: learned from a real cook
li.description: A traveling cook spent a whole day teaching me. I hold a knife differently now.

li.label: a healer saw to me
li.description: A traveling healer looked me over, knew what it was straight away, and the council paid for the cure. It's easing already.

li.label: someone played just for me
li.description: A musician sat out by the woodpile with me and played slow tunes until I fell asleep where I sat.

li.label: they came to see how we decide
li.description: Envoys came all the way from a neighbor's town to watch our council decide things, and wrote down every word.

li.label: a taste of home
li.description: A peddler had food from where I grew up, and the council bought it for me. The smell alone took me straight back.

li.label: a supper from someone's home
li.description: We ate a supper from someone else's homeland, with the story of every dish. I'd have the sour one again.

li.label: made peace with an old enemy
li.description: The one who wronged me, years before the colony, turned up at the gate to say sorry. We talked behind a closed door most of the afternoon.

li.label: an old wound reopened
li.description: Someone from my old life came to apologize, and it only brought it all back. I shouldn't have let them in.

li.label: our dead have proper markers
li.description: Every grave has a proper marker now, with the name cut in stone. I read them all on my way past.

li.label: a feast at the camp
li.description: We spent the evening at the camp's fire with their people, eating out of the same pot.

li.label: the council backed me
li.description: I had a quarrel with someone from the camp, and the council came down on my side. They went back with a face like thunder.

li.label: the council gave it away
li.description: I had the better claim, and the council let the camp have it anyway, to keep the peace.
